answer: Bind identities to place. Beacons on ferrous masts (a ridge site, one knoll, line-of-sight) issue unpredictable challenges; consensus times round-trip replies to ≥3 of them, resolving each key to one terrain cell — one credential per cell per epoch. Clones stacked at one site share that cell — extra headcount earns nothing; each new identity needs a physical responder at a new site, at linear cost: per-epoch rent plus amortized receiver. Deters only while per-cell reward sits below that cost; assumes an honest beacon majority; rural cells stay cheaply farmable.
